summary:
CoastWatch is an interactive coastal observation explorer designed to help users explore coastal surface changes around Alappuzha, Kerala, using NISAR (NASA Aperture Radar) satellite observations.

The platform provides an interactive dashboard with observation date selection, HH/HV polarisation information, product metadata, coverage-footprint visualisation, browse-image previews and JSON export. It aims to make satellite observation data more accessible and support the exploration and understanding of coastal environmental changes.

Currently, CoastWatch is a functional prototype focused on NISAR product exploration. Integration of actual GCOV raster data, automated shoreline extraction and validated coastal-change analysis are planned for future development.
details:
Project Details — Coastwatch

What does the project do and how does it work?

Coastwatch is an interactive coastal observation explorer designed to help users explore coastal surface changes around Alappuzha, Kerala, using NISAR (NASA-Aperture Radar) satellite observations.

The application provides a dashboard where users can explore available satellite observation dates, view HH and HV polarization information, inspect product metadata and coverage footprints, and browse corresponding satellite-image previews. Users can switch between observations, explore the map and export selected observation information as a JSON file.

Our approach focuses on making complex Earth observation information easier to explore and understand through an accessible, interactive interface.

What benefits does it provide?

Coastal regions such as Alappuzha are exposed to environmental processes including coastal erosion, flooding and sediment movement. Understanding these changes is important for coastal planning, environmental awareness and disaster preparedness.

Coastwatch aims to make satellite observation products more accessible to students, researchers and people interested in coastal environments. By presenting observation information through maps, visual previews and structured metadata, the platform provides a foundation for exploring coastal conditions over time.

What is the intended impact?

Our long-term vision is to support better understanding and monitoring of coastal environments through satellite-based Earth observation.

CoastWatch could eventually help researchers, students, environmental organizations and coastal communities explore changes in coastal landscapes and identify areas that may require further investigation.

Future development will focus on integrating actual georeferenced NISAR GCOV raster data, developing land-water classification techniques, extracting shoreline boundaries and validating coastal-change measurements.

What tools and technologies were used?

Our team developed the project using:

- *React.js* – Building the interactive frontend.

- *JavaScript* – Application logic and interactive functionality.

- *HTML and CSS* – Structuring and styling the interface.

- *Leaflet* – Interactive map visualisation.

- *Vite* – Development environment and application build tooling.

- *GitHub* – Source-code management and collaboration.

- *Vercel*– Hosting and deployment of the web application.

- *NASA–NISAR data products* – Satellite observation products used as the project's intended data source.

- *AI-assisted development tools* – Supporting software development, debugging and project planning.

What makes the project creative?

CoastWatch combines satellite observation information, interactive mapping and an accessible dashboard into a single exploration platform.

Rather than presenting satellite products as complicated technical files, the application aims to make them easier to navigate through observation selectors, polarisation information, map-based coverage visualisation and image previews.

The project also focuses on a specific coastal study area, Alappuzha, connecting advanced satellite Earth observation technology with a regional environmental challenge.

What factors did the team consider?

During development, we considered data accessibility, ease of use, geographical relevance, visual clarity, technical feasibility and scientific reliability.

We also considered the importance of distinguishing actual satellite observations from illustrative previews and product coverage from extracted shoreline boundaries.

At the current prototype stage, the existing browse images and coverage footprint support product exploration; the HDF5 GCOV datasets have not yet been independently processed or validated. Therefore, CoastWatch does not currently claim measured shoreline displacement or erosion rates.

Our next objective is to integrate the actual satellite datasets and develop a scientifically validated coastal-change analysis workflow.
